analysis.title: 'Nothing Was Spared': After A Week When Everything Got Liquidated, Goldman Asks Is The Commodity Puke Over?
key_insights: Commodities were hit by two sequential shocks: a hawkish Fed and strong-dollar repricing that lifted real rates, then an AI-equity deleveraging that forced liquidation across commodities irrespective of the dollar. No BCOM sector was spared.

The most crowded markets fell hardest with no headline: UK emissions -10% from the 98th percentile of 3-year positioning, sugar -8% from the 92nd percentile. Silver fell 16% on the week and copper 10%.
Precious metals and energy were each down roughly 14% over 20 days (read off a chart, approximate).
Copper fell 10% on growth fears, bearish Chinese demand feedback from CESCO, and US export expectations that triggered heavy SHFE short-selling. The desk came into China with a modest short.

Goldman admits it underestimated how easily trade houses diverted metal to China (CESCO feedback >100k MT for Dec) and how negative Chinese demand sentiment is. It estimates the US over-imported 1.7mn MT since Jan24, and small recent exports show a release valve.

Chinese physical copper is the tightest in 15 years (cash arb +$750/mt, SHFE curve inverted, domestic inventories -70% YoY), but Goldman says China tightness is 'at best tangential to price'. The bull counter is AI capex, tight scrap, no 2027 mine supply rebound and State Grid tenders.

Gold is 34% off the year's highs and had its worst week since March. The sell-off is more orderly than January, with positioning balanced in aggregate. The CTA model shows further selling in flat or down tapes despite a large short, and ETF positioning is high but sticky.

SHFE gold open interest shed 8.5k lots Friday, a 95th-percentile one-day drop. There is a growing physical bid from India and Turkey. Robert Quinn's 4-5 sigma panic signal historically reverses within a week, which conflicts with the CTA view.
1-month gold vol rose about 7 vols on the week with riskies 2 vols further toward puts. There is little macro interest to re-engage and Goldman's own gold delta is small short to flat.

Goldman's 2027 outlook expects near-term gold downside and high vol while the Fed keeps hiking, then gold at $4,650 by end-2027 and $5,600 by end-2028 once cuts begin. Silver is expected to underperform gold through the hiking cycle.

Crude was soft as the Trump-Putin-Xi meeting signaled no imminent escalation, and rallies were capped by macro weakness. Physical looks to have found a floor, with DFLs flat and North Sea diffs slightly higher.

12-month Brent vol is in the 100th percentile of its 3-year history while 12-month 25-delta put skew is in only the 8th percentile. The desk is short vol, expects realised vol compression to persist, but likes owning front call spreads to guard against an escalation rally.
Goldman's 2027 oil outlook sees Brent averaging $88 next year and $78 by December 2027 as Hormuz bypass routes let the market adapt.

TTF options OI is massive at nearly every strike from 40 to 125 EUR, particularly Dec, and holders run them live, leaving the market very short gamma. October's rally was orderly until 100 EUR, then turned violent.

Hormuz LNG crossings have averaged over 60% of pre-war levels month-to-date and January JKM basis is weak. Yarrow expects Q1 to be highly volatile and says it is too early to fade given the right tail.

Goldman's longer-term TTF bear trade is in the back end. Summer-29 trades near 28 EUR/MWh versus a downside target in the high teens to low 20s, and the desk suggests layering into Summer-28 and Summer-29 downside via max-loss structures.
Author leans toward the CTA view that systematic selling is not done until the AI unwind finds a floor. With the Fed still hiking, the real asset trade may wait for cuts.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term downside and high vol while the Fed hikes, with CTAs still selling. Silver expected to underperform gold.
Tight Chinese physical market is offset by easy metal diversion, weak demand sentiment and US export release valve.
Short vol bias with front call spreads as protection. Brent seen at $88 average in 2027 amid a glut.
Back-end Summer-28 and Summer-29 embed a scarcity premium, with new LNG supply coming. Front is volatile with a right tail.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Structural central-bank buying supports gold once the Fed begins cutting, but near-term downside persists.
Goldman sees a glut as Gulf barrels return, which supports fading far-dated vol.
Higher real rates pressure gold and silver and drive liquidation across commodities.

trade_ideas.description: Own front-month Brent call spreads while staying short far-dated (6-12 month) vol
trade_ideas.rationale: Realised vol is compressing and the market looks past skirmishes, but front call spreads protect against an escalation-driven rally.
trade_ideas.risk: Strike on Iran arriving earlier than the 'after the new year' timing, causing a spike.

trade_ideas.description: Layer into short TTF Summer-28 and Summer-29 via max-loss structures
trade_ideas.rationale: Back end embeds a scarcity premium not justified by fundamentals given new LNG capacity from 2025-26 FIDs.
trade_ideas.risk: Weather and timing in Q1, and a right tail in front-end gas.

risk_factors: Further AI-equity deleveraging could force more commodity liquidation.
Continued Fed hikes keep real rates high and pressure precious metals.
Escalation involving Iran, including strikes on vessels or US bases, could spike oil.
Further CTA selling in gold unless price rips higher.
US copper exports adding supply to a weak Chinese demand backdrop.
Weather and timing in TTF Q1 with a short gamma market.
charts_described: Chart of commodity sector performance over 20 days shows precious metals and energy each down roughly 14%, with approximate figures read off the chart per the text.
Chart of US copper imports shows they ran well above the pre-tariff monthly average, at times nearly triple, over the past 18 months, then fell sharply.
vol_and_positioning: 1-month gold vol rose about 7 vols on the week, riskies 2 vols further toward puts. Little macro interest to re-engage, a few specialists buying upside in small size.
12-month Brent vol in the 100th percentile of its 3-year history, 12-month 25-delta put skew in the 8th percentile. Traders are rolling front positions into the 6-12 month bucket.
Goldman oil desk is short vol, but likes owning front-month call spreads to guard against an escalation-driven rally.
TTF market is very short gamma, with massive options OI from 40 to 125 EUR and holders running options live.
UK emissions positioning was in the 98th percentile and sugar in the 92nd percentile before the sell-off.
CTA model shows further gold selling in flat or down tapes with small covering on a sharp move higher. ETF positioning is high but sticky.
SHFE gold OI fell 8.5k lots Friday, a 95th-percentile one-day drop.
Palladium is extremely short and finding cost-curve support at 5-year lows.
geopolitical: Trump-Putin-Xi meeting read as a sign escalation was not imminent, weighing on crude.
Reports that Washington is weighing fresh strikes on Iran, and that Iran will respond if its vessels are attacked.
Trump cited on Fox as inclined to strike Iran after the new year if there is no deal.
Iran hitting US bases in Bahrain, noted in the closing paragraph.
Hormuz LNG flows recovering to over 60% of pre-war levels, and Hormuz-bypass pipelines aiding oil adaptation.
Possible US administration trade stance (described as 'presumably' proactive) affecting the copper bull case.
cross_bank_references: UBS trading desk warned to 'watch for AI fears to morph into a broader growth scare across assets'.
UBS Wealth Management called the copper drop a sentiment and inventory story with fundamentals intact.
